questions.question: What do you write to get a working repository for the Meal entity with a Long id?
options: An empty interface that extends JpaRepository<Meal, Long>
A class with save and find methods written by hand
An abstract class that extends Meal
A @Service that opens its own connection
questions.explanation: Spring Data builds the implementation at startup, so an empty interface is enough.

questions.question: What does save() do when the entity already has an id that exists in the table?
options: It always inserts a second row
It throws a duplicate key error
It deletes the row and stops
questions.explanation: save() inserts new entities and updates existing ones, so the same method covers both cases.

questions.question: The table holds 4 meals. The code calls deleteById(2L) and then prints repository.count(). What is printed?
questions.explanation: Deleting one row leaves three, and count() returns the number of remaining rows.

questions.question: A developer writes repository.findAll(Sort.by("unit_price")) on an entity with the field unitPrice. What happens?
options: It sorts by the column and works
It fails, because Sort uses Java field names, not column names
questions.explanation: Sort.by expects the entity property name, so use unitPrice.

questions.question: A page shows every product by calling findAll() on a table with millions of rows. What is the risk?
options: It loads all rows into memory, so use findAll(Pageable) instead
It returns only the first ten rows
questions.explanation: findAll() has no limit, so a big table can use too much memory and time.
